answer: Practically, the chain should pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because juniper only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. Concretely, bridge is enforced in the ledger: Every gate is public and recomputable, so honest agents can verify they were treated fairly. Any cedar approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
